questions.text:
Consider the following table named Student in a relational database. The primary key of this table is rollNum.
[latex]\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|} \hline \\ rollNum&name&gender&marks \\ \hline 1&Naman&M&62\\ \hline 2&Aliya&F&70 \\ \hline 3&Aliya &F&80 \\ \hline 4&James&M&82\\ \hline 5&Swati&F&65\\ \hline \end{array} [/latex]
The SQL query below is executed on this database.

SELECT *
FROM Student
WHERE gender = 'F' AND
 marks > 65;

The number of rows returned by the query is ______
questions.solution:
Rows with gender = 'F' and marks [latex]\gt[/latex] 65:
- Aliya, 70 True
- Aliya, 80 True
- Swati, 65 False (65 is not greater than 65)

SELECT * returns full rows, so the duplicate name does not matter.

Answer: 2

questions.text:
Consider a database of fixed-length records, stored as an ordered file. The database has 25,000 records, with each record being 100 bytes, of which the primary key occupies 15 bytes. The data file is block-aligned in that each data record is fully contained within a block. The database is indexed by a primary index file, which is also stored as a block-aligned ordered file. The figure below depicts this indexing scheme.

Suppose the block size of the file system is 1024 bytes, and a pointer to a block occupies 5 bytes. The system uses binary search on the index file to search for a record with a given key. You may assume that a binary search on an index file of [latex]b[/latex] blocks takes [latex]\left \lceil \log_2 b \right \rceil [/latex] block accesses in the worst case.
Given a key, the number of block accesses required to identify the block in the data file that may contain a record with the key, in the worst case, is _____
questions.solution:
Compute the index size step by step:
- Records per data block = [latex]\lfloor1024/100\rfloor=10[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] data blocks = 25000 / 10 = 2500.
- Primary (sparse) index has one entry per data block: 2500 entries of [latex]15+5=20[/latex] bytes.
- Entries per index block = [latex]\lfloor1024/20\rfloor=51[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] index blocks = [latex]\lceil2500/51\rceil=50[/latex].

Binary search on the index: [latex]\lceil\log_2 50\rceil=6[/latex] block accesses identify the data block.

Answer: 6

questions.text:
Consider the language L over the alphabet {0, 1}, given below:

[latex]L = \{w \in \{0, 1\}^* | w \text{ does not contain three or more consecutive 1's} \}.[/latex]
The minimum number of states in a Deterministic Finite-State Automaton (DFA) for L is _____.
questions.solution:
The DFA only needs to remember how many 1s have just been seen in a row:
- q0: last symbol 0 (or start)
- q1: one 1
- q2: two 1s
- q3: three 1s seen [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] dead (non-final) state

q0, q1, q2 are final. A 0 returns q0/q1/q2 to q0. All 4 states are distinguishable.

Answer: 4

questions.text:
An 8-way set associative cache of size 64 KB (1 KB = 1024 bytes) is used in a system with 32-bit address. The address is sub-divided into TAG, INDEX, and BLOCK OFFSET.
The number of bits in the TAG is ____.
questions.solution:
Size of one way [latex]=\frac{64\text{ KB}}{8}=8\text{ KB}=2^{13}[/latex] bytes.

INDEX + OFFSET bits together address one way, so they total 13 bits (the block size does not matter).

TAG [latex]=32-13=19[/latex] bits

Answer: 19

questions.text:
The forwarding table of a router is shown below.
[latex]\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|} \hline \\ Subnet \; Number&Subnet \;Mask&Interface ID \\ \hline 200.150.0.0 &255.255.0.0& 1\\ \hline 200.150.64.0 &255.255.224.0 &2\\ \hline 200.150.68.0 &255.255.255.0 &3\\ \hline 200.150.68.64 &255.255.255.224 &4 \\ \hline Default & &0\\ \hline \end{array} [/latex]
A packet addressed to a destination address 200.150.68.118 arrives at the router. It will be forwarded to the interface with ID _____.
questions.solution:
Check each entry for 200.150.68.118 (longest prefix wins):
- 200.150.0.0/16 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] matches
- 200.150.64.0/19 (third octet 64-95) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 68 matches
- 200.150.68.0/24 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] matches
- 200.150.68.64/27 (last octet 64-95) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 118 does not match

Longest match is /24 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] interface 3.

Answer: 3
